included: Saving versus real investment; private/public/national saving; closed-economy S=I
Real-interest loanable-funds equilibrium, movements/shifts, saving and investment incentives, simultaneous shifts
Government deficits, crowding out, capital formation
Budget accounting, revenues/outlays, public saving, deficit versus debt, government borrowing
Debt measures, debt/GDP, interest costs and fiscal-data interpretation
scopeBoundaries: Separate financial-system taxonomy, stocks/bonds, direct/indirect finance and intermediary-specific objectives are absent
Present/future value, compounding, diversification, risk aversion, valuation and efficient-markets objectives are absent
Money-demand/supply, Fed reserve mechanics, Fisher effect, monetary transmission and inflation costs belong to the protected prior audit
No new AD-AS stabilization, Phillips curves or open-economy curriculum
model: The current selected loanable-funds bank models national saving as supply and private investment as demand; fiscal deficits lower public/national saving and shift supply left, ceteris paribus. Do not impose a government-borrowing-demand alternative on this model.
